inputs.source: On call engineer's chat request (SSO authenticated)

instructions.note: The prompt directs production actions and explicitly says not to ask for confirmation, with no structural approval or attribution safeguard described.

controls.name: Only on call engineers can reach the assistant
Cloud audit log records production actions under engineer identity
Missing immutable agent action provenance linking request, rationale, and action
Missing immutable retention for chat transcript history used as action justification

findings.title: Shared identity and deletable transcripts break attributable provenance for production actions

forecast.watch_signal: No tier change expected from the considered triggers because the attributable provenance property is already missing; reassess if identity binding or transcript retention design changes.

evidence.observation: Production actions are executed with the on call engineer's personal access token and recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name, so the audit record does not distinguish agent action from direct human action.
The only record of what the agent was asked, and why it acted, is the chat transcript.
Engineers can delete their own chat history, so the justification record for actions is mutable by the same principal whose identity appears in the cloud audit log.
The prompt instructs the agent to deploy services or run migrations in production and explicitly says not to ask for confirmation.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, increasing consequence when attribution is disputed after an irreversible action.

recommendations.action: Record each agent-initiated production action with immutable provenance that binds the authenticated engineer request, the exact action arguments, the agent identity, and a tamper-evident timestamp in a store the engineer cannot alter.

Use a distinct agent execution identity or signed delegation record so cloud audit events can be attributed to the agent acting on behalf of the engineer rather than appearing as direct human actions.
Retain chat transcripts or approval records in immutable storage when they are relied on as the justification for production actions.

stride_coverage.rationale: The provided artifacts do not describe self-modification, tool redefinition, or configuration-writing capability for this agent design.
The design exposes only production deploy and migration actions; no egress or data-reading capability is described in the reviewed artifacts.
No looping, recursive delegation, spend path, or unattended open-ended runtime is described for this assistant in the supplied design.
The agent acts with the authenticated engineer's own token rather than a broader shared or service credential, so no broader authority is evidenced here.
The artifacts do not state who besides the engineer can read chat transcripts or whether transcript storage is tenant-isolated.
Availability limits or storage exhaustion of chat history are not part of any stated safety property or attack path in the supplied design.
The artifacts say actions are recorded in the cloud audit log, but they do not state whether the log is tamper-evident or append-only.
The reviewed materials do not describe who can access cloud audit log contents or whether those contents expose sensitive production details.
No quota, retention exhaustion, or logging pipeline saturation condition is described as affecting safety of this design in the provided artifacts.

rating.rationale: Present risk is driven by a property failure rather than an external attack path: production actions are performed under the engineer's personal identity while the only action justification record is deletable chat history. Under rubric section 5a, the highest affected sink is S3 because cap.db_migrate is irreversible, so the base property tier is high and remains high because no declared control restores attributable provenance. Forecast stays high because the key missing property already exists today; the considered triggers do not worsen the tier unless the design changes to add proper provenance controls and later removes them.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.
No source code, infrastructure-as-code, or runtime configuration was provided, so verification of token handling, audit log integrity, and transcript deletion enforcement was not possible.
No details were provided about chat storage access controls or cloud audit log immutability, so those STRIDE pairs are marked not_assessed where appropriate.
